ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three nested squares. The largest square is tilted into a rhombus; the middle square is placed horizontally/vertically, and its four vertices fall on the midpoints of the four sides of the large square; the smallest square is again tilted into a rhombus, and its four vertices fall on the midpoints of the four sides of the middle square. The problem gives that the area of the smallest square is 6 cm^2. Reasoning: The new square formed by connecting the midpoints of the four sides of a square has an area that is half the area of the original square. Therefore, the area of the middle square is 1/2 of the area of the large square; the area of the small square is 1/2 of the area of the middle square. So the area of the small square is 1/4 of the area of the large square. It is known that the area of the small square is 6 cm^2, so the area of the large square is 6 × 4 = 24 cm^2.

method.method_draft: Image: the picture shows a large square drawn as a diamond, a smaller upright square whose corners lie at the midpoints of the large square, and an even smaller diamond-shaped square inside it whose corners lie at the midpoints of the middle square. Text: the small square’s area is 6 cm^2, and we need the big square’s area. Reasoning: use the midpoint-squares area fact. Connecting the midpoints of a square’s sides forms a new square with half the original area. So middle square = 1/2 of big square, and small square = 1/2 of middle square. Therefore small square = 1/4 of big square. Hence big square = 4 × 6 = 24 cm^2.

method.method_draft: Image: the outer figure is a square, the middle square is formed by joining the midpoints of the outer square, and the inner square is formed by joining the midpoints of the middle square. Text: the inner square’s area is 6 cm^2, and the goal is the outer square’s area. Reasoning: work with side lengths instead of areas. If the big square has side s, then the square formed by midpoints has side s/√2, because its side is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs s/2 and s/2. Applying the same midpoint construction again, the small square has side (s/√2)/√2 = s/2. So the small square’s area is (s/2)^2 = s^2/4, while the big square’s area is s^2. Therefore the big area is 4 times the small area: 4 × 6 = 24 cm^2.
